Ouches
OW-chez
noun
Middle English ouche, a brooch or jewelled setting (from Old French nouche); rendering Hebrew mishbetsōth, the wrought settings of gold in which the stones of the high priest’s ephod were fixed.

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

📖 Biblical Definition

Ouches are the settings of gold — sockets of wreathen, embroidered work — that held the precious stones upon the high priest’s shoulders. Upon two onyx stones were graven the names of the children of Israel, six on the one and six on the other, “with the work of an engraver in stone, like the engravings of a signet”; and the LORD commanded, “thou shalt make them to be set in ouches of gold” (Exo 28:11). So set, the stones were fastened on the shoulders of the ephod, “for stones of memorial unto the children of Israel: and Aaron shall bear their names before the LORD upon his two shoulders for a memorial” (Exo 28:12). The ouches also received the wreathen chains that bound on the breastplate (Exo 28:25). Mark what the ouches did: they held the names of the people fast to the priest, so that Israel could not slip from his shoulders while he stood before God. Here is the believer’s security in his great High Priest. The names of Christ’s people are not laid loosely upon Him but set in Him as stones in gold — graven like a signet, fixed in a setting that cannot fail. He bears His own upon the shoulders of His strength before the face of God, and none shall pluck them thence.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The gold settings that held the engraved memorial stones upon the high priest’s shoulders; the fastness of the saints’ names upon their Priest.

expand to see more

OUCHES, sockets or settings of wrought gold, in which precious stones were fixed.

The two onyx stones graven with Israel’s names were set in ouches of gold upon the ephod.

The wreathen chains of the breastplate were also fastened in the ouches.

By them Aaron bore the names of the children of Israel before the LORD for a memorial.

They figure the fastness of the saints’ names, set like signet-graven stones in Christ.

📖 Key Scripture

Exo 28:11 — "With the work of an engraver in stone, like the engravings of a signet, shalt thou engrave the two stones with the names of the children of Israel: thou shalt make them to be set in ouches of gold."

Exo 28:12 — "And thou shalt put the two stones upon the shoulders of the ephod for stones of memorial unto the children of Israel: and Aaron shall bear their names before the LORD upon his two shoulders for a memorial."

Exo 28:25 — "And the other two ends of the two wreathen chains thou shalt fasten in the two ouches, and put them on the shoulderpieces of the ephod before it."

Joh 10:28 — "And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A setting of the sanctuary, not a contested doctrine; it recovers the fastness of the believer’s name upon his High Priest — set in gold, not laid on loosely.

expand to see more

Ouches face no postmodern redefinition. The truth they carry answers the trembling saint who fears he may yet slip from the memory or the mercy of God — as though his name were laid loosely upon Christ and might fall in a rough hour.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the security of the saints in their Priest. The names were graven like a signet — cut in, not written on — and then set in ouches of gold so the stones could not drop. So Christ bears His people: engraved and set, carried on the shoulders of His strength before the face of God, and none shall pluck them out of His hand.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Middle English for a jewelled setting, ouches render the gold sockets that fixed Israel’s engraved memorial stones on the high priest’s ephod.

expand to see more

Ouches — Middle English ouche, a brooch or setting; Hebrew mishbetsōth.

They held the two onyx stones graven with Israel’s twelve names.

They were fixed on the shoulderpieces of the ephod (Exo 28:12).

The wreathen chains of the breastplate fastened into them.

They figure the saints’ names set fast in Christ their Priest.

Usage

"The names of Christ’s people are set in Him as stones in gold, graven like a signet."

"Israel could not slip from the priest’s shoulders while he stood before God."

"He bears His own upon the shoulders of His strength, and none shall pluck them thence."
